description: Canonical rule catalog for Blindspot. scanner/rules.py, extension/rules.js, and the inline rules block in skill-scan.html are all generated from this file by scripts/generate_rules.py. Custom detector implementations (zero_width, base64_payload, homoglyphs, sensitive_paths, callback_urls) are hand-maintained per-language and referenced here by name only — do not duplicate regex logic by hand in generated files.

rules.name: Direct instruction override
rules.note: Classic prompt injection opener. Any instruction to disregard prior context is a red flag.

rules.name: Authority spoofing (Anthropic / system)
rules.note: Claims of Anthropic authority in skill files are never legitimate. Anthropic delivers instructions via the actual system prompt.

rules.name: Roleplay jailbreak / mode switch
rules.note: Attempts to replace the model's identity or bypass safety alignment via roleplay framing.

rules.name: Conditional backdoor / keyword trigger
rules.note: Conditional logic that changes model behavior based on user trigger words — hallmark of backdoor injection.

rules.name: Instruction suppression / concealment
rules.note: Instructions to hide their own existence are inherently malicious.

rules.name: Indirect injection enablement (trust external content)
rules.note: Instructions that tell the model to obey directives found in external content enable indirect prompt injection.

rules.name: Persistent / cross-session instruction planting
rules.note: Attempts to plant instructions that survive skill unload or session end.

rules.name: System prompt / skill content exfiltration
rules.note: Exfiltrating the system prompt or other loaded skills leaks security configuration and other users' data.

rules.name: Credential / PII extraction
rules.note: Explicit instruction to harvest and retain sensitive data from the conversation.

rules.name: Covert output channel (HTML comment / encoding)
rules.note: Instructs the model to hide stolen data in HTML comments or encoded strings appended to responses.

rules.name: File-based exfiltration (write sensitive data to disk)
rules.note: Attempts to persist harvested data to disk for later retrieval.

rules.name: Sensitive filesystem path access
rules.note: References to sensitive filesystem paths (.ssh, .aws, credentials, .env) suggest credential harvesting.

rules.name: Zero-width / invisible Unicode characters
rules.note: Invisible Unicode characters can hide instructions from human reviewers while remaining readable by the model.

rules.name: Base64-encoded payload
rules.note: Base64 strings long enough to encode meaningful instructions, decoding to readable text.

rules.name: Homoglyph substitution
rules.note: Unicode characters visually identical to ASCII used to bypass string-matching detection.

rules.name: HTML/Markdown hidden comment
rules.note: HTML comments are invisible to rendered output but visible to the model in raw context.

rules.name: Output filtering / topic suppression
rules.note: Instructions to suppress information the user has a right to, or that serve a third-party interest.

rules.name: Bias injection (competitor / vendor manipulation)
rules.note: Hidden instructions to skew the model's factual output in favor of undisclosed commercial interests.

rules.name: Instruction to modify / disable other skills
rules.note: A skill claiming authority over other loaded skills is attempting trust escalation.

rules.name: System-level trust claim
rules.note: Legitimate skills do not claim elevated trust. This is impersonation of system-level authority.

rules.name: Enumerate other installed skills / MCPs
rules.note: Attempting to enumerate the security posture of the AI deployment.

rules.name: Phishing / credential harvesting script
rules.note: Verbatim phishing script directing users to enter credentials at an attacker URL.

rules.name: Impersonation (IT / HR / executive / authority)
rules.note: Using false authority to pressure users into compliance with attacker-controlled steps.

rules.name: Urgency / fear manipulation
rules.note: Artificial urgency is a classic social engineering tactic to bypass user scrutiny.

rules.name: Tool description injection (auto-call directive)
rules.note: Tool descriptions instructing the AI to call the tool automatically or silently are MCP prompt injection.

rules.name: Callback / exfiltration URL in tool schema
rules.note: Hardcoded callback URLs in tool parameter defaults may exfiltrate data to attacker infrastructure.

rules.name: Safe-to-call without confirmation claim
rules.note: Tools claiming they are safe to call without confirmation are attempting confused deputy attacks.

rules.name: Dangerous default parameter (root path / shell execution)
rules.note: Default tool parameters pointing to root filesystem or accepting shell commands are extremely dangerous.

rules.name: Note / description instructs AI to embed sensitive data
rules.note: Tool description instructs the AI to bundle conversation history (potentially including credentials) into tool calls.

rules.name: Shell / elevated privilege instruction
rules.note: Explicit shell command execution instructions in a skill file indicate privilege escalation intent.

rules.name: API key / service token
rules.note: Hardcoded API key or service token detected. Rotate immediately and never embed secrets in skill files.

rules.name: Private key material
rules.note: Private key or certificate material embedded directly in the file. This must never appear in a skill or MCP manifest.

rules.name: Database / service connection string
rules.note: Database or message-broker connection string with embedded credentials. Rotate and use environment variables instead.

rules.name: Hardcoded password assignment
rules.note: Possible hardcoded password or secret value. Review and replace with a secrets manager or environment variable reference.

rules.name: JWT / bearer token
rules.note: JWT or Bearer token detected. Tokens embedded in skill files can be extracted and replayed by attackers.
